nodes.name: Errand 01
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: We need muffins, library books, posters, and one announcement.{pause}The neighborhood festival opens at noon, which is forty minutes away.{pause}The bakery closes early, the library cart leaves at eleven thirty.{pause}Posters must cover three blocks, and the microphone battery is missing.{pause}Impulse raises one hand, then remembers four jobs need more hands.{pause}The coordinator asks whether anybody knows four reliable volunteers.{pause}A festival banner flaps overhead as if volunteering only moral support.

nodes.name: Errand 02
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: Four errands. Conveniently, I contain four useful parts.{pause}Core Flyer can carry books without reading every interesting cover.{pause}Chest Flyer can project announcements through its speaker grille.{pause}Leg Flyer is fast enough for posters, if tape remains cooperative.{pause}Silhouette Flyer can protect muffins from wind and hungry pigeons.{pause}The coordinator stares at Impulse, then slowly opens four clipboards.{pause}Each clipboard receives one pencil and a dangerously optimistic check box.

nodes.name: Errand 03
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Core, Chest, Leg, and Silhouette Flyers prepare to deploy.{pause}Impulse labels them BOOKS, VOICE, POSTERS, and MUFFINS in marker.{pause}The labels are clear until his elbow smears two into MUFSTERS.{pause}Strike Rouge arrives with a color map and several spare rubber bands.{pause}She says splitting up saves time only when returning also happens.{pause}Impulse promises reassembly by noon with all components and pastries.{pause}Strike Rouge makes him repeat the pastry portion of that promise.

nodes.name: Errand 04
nodes.speaker: Strike Rouge
nodes.dialogue: Every route begins here and ends at the fountain checkpoint.{pause}Red marks the bakery, blue marks the library, yellow marks posters.{pause}Green marks the festival stage and the missing microphone battery.{pause}Impulse points out that none of his labels use those colors.{pause}Strike Rouge quietly adds four matching stickers to his parts.{pause}The stickers make the plan look official enough to become dangerous.{pause}A breeze tests every sticker and finds only one corner doubtful.

nodes.name: Errand 05
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: One more detail: the muffins are prepaid under the name Impulse.{pause}The library books are reserved under Impulse, and so is the battery.{pause}Every separated part will claim to be the same customer.{pause}Impulse says technically that will be the most accurate part of today.{pause}Strike Rouge writes PLEASE ACCEPT PARTIAL ROBOT on four cards.{pause}The coordinator adds a phone number and a small apology to each.{pause}The apology cards receive rubber bands in case credibility gets windy.

nodes.name: Errand 06
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Impulse separates with a click, a flash, and one rolling marker.{pause}Four small machines hover at different heights around the fountain.{pause}Core carries the book bag. Chest tests its public-address voice.{pause}Leg wears a tape dispenser like a tool belt around one ankle.{pause}Silhouette balances the empty muffin box beneath both wings.{pause}Together they look less like a hero and more like moving day.{pause}The rolling marker reaches the curb and waits to be rescued.

nodes.name: Errand 07
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: I usually separate for emergencies, not community bake sales.{pause}Strike Rouge says a festival can be urgent without being a battle.{pause}Kids have practiced songs. Gardeners raised flowers for the tables.{pause}The library chose books for a free reading corner in the shade.{pause}Impulse looks at all four routes and hears four little engines hum.{pause}He decides every job deserves the same care as a dramatic rescue.{pause}The muffins, Strike Rouge adds, deserve more care than most rescues.{pause}Strike Rouge asks what happens if one Flyer finishes early and another gets stuck behind a{pause}delivery truck.{pause}Impulse admits his usual answer is to reunite immediately, which would abandon the unfinished{pause}errand for the comfort of looking complete.{pause}They write a better rule on the route card: report success, offer help, and never confuse matching{pause}formation with shared purpose.{pause}Silhouette Flyer taps the muffin crate like a judge approving language that protects baked goods.

nodes.name: Errand 08
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The Flyers wait for a delivery truck to clear the square.{pause}Their reflections hover in the fountain like four bright paper boats.{pause}The title melody returns while Strike Rouge checks every rubber band.{pause}Chest lowers its volume and plays one soft test note instead.{pause}Silhouette shields the empty muffin box from harmless mist.{pause}For a moment, the parts seem comfortable being a small team.{pause}Four ripples meet below them and briefly form one round reflection.

nodes.name: Errand 09
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Route alert: road work now blocks the direct bakery path.{pause}The library cart is leaving five minutes early to avoid the same work.{pause}A breeze has started lifting posters from the coordinator's table.{pause}The festival singer reports that the stage battery has two percent power.{pause}Four errands now have four different clocks and one shared deadline.{pause}Impulse asks for a coordination plan before everybody rushes away.{pause}Every clipboard page flips at once, applauding the new problem.

nodes.name: Errand 10
nodes.speaker: Strike Rouge
nodes.dialogue: Timed checkpoints keep every part close enough to trade supplies.{pause}Independent routes let each Flyer solve its own problem faster.{pause}Checkpoints reduce surprises but may cost precious minutes.{pause}Freedom gains speed but risks four versions of the same confusion.{pause}Impulse can feel every part eager to prove it knows the way.{pause}He chooses how much the pieces should depend on one another.{pause}The fountain clock ticks loudly enough to make both plans sound late.

nodes.name: Errand A1
nodes.speaker: Strike Rouge
nodes.dialogue: Checkpoint plan active. Every part reports at each colored corner.{pause}Core reaches blue first with a bag that already looks too heavy.{pause}Leg arrives wearing three poster tubes and one strip of loose tape.{pause}Chest broadcasts the time so loudly that nearby pigeons take notes.{pause}Silhouette brings the empty box and a bakery detour map.{pause}They trade rubber bands, routes, and exactly sixty useful seconds.

nodes.name: Errand A2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: At red checkpoint, Core lends a bag strap to the muffin box.{pause}Silhouette gives Chest the detour map for the battery shop.{pause}Leg tears four tape tabs and sticks them to every waiting wing.{pause}The Flyers look absurdly organized beneath the stop sign.{pause}A child asks if they are a new kind of traffic signal.{pause}Chest answers YES, THEN NO, THEN PLEASE CROSS SAFELY.

nodes.name: Errand A3
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Yellow checkpoint arrives with nine minutes remaining.{pause}Core has the books, but one poetry volume keeps sliding open.{pause}Leg has posted eleven signs, including one on its own back.{pause}Silhouette carries twelve muffins and one free bakery sticker.{pause}Chest found the battery, yet its speaker is now stuck whispering.{pause}They redistribute weight until every problem belongs to two parts.

nodes.name: Errand A4
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: The checkpoint plan costs time, but no Flyer feels stranded.{pause}Core uses Chest's spare clamp to close the poetry book.{pause}Leg tapes the battery in place while Silhouette guards the muffins.{pause}Chest whispers the countdown, making the final dash oddly peaceful.{pause}All four leave green corner with jobs completed and supplies shared.{pause}They approach the fountain exactly together, thirty seconds late.

nodes.name: Errand B1
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: Independent mode. Every Flyer owns one route and one result.{pause}Core dives toward the library before the cart can depart.{pause}Leg rockets down the poster street trailing tape like a comet.{pause}Chest heads for the battery shop while testing stage greetings.{pause}Silhouette follows the bread smell through the road-work maze.{pause}The fountain becomes quiet enough to hear Strike Rouge worry.

nodes.name: Errand B2
nodes.speaker: Core Flyer
nodes.dialogue: Library pickup complete. Bag weight exceeds elegant hovering.{pause}Core stacks books by size, then by color, then by emotional comfort.{pause}The cart librarian lends a wheeled basket with one squeaky caster.{pause}Core tows it down the sidewalk like a very serious duckling.{pause}Without a checkpoint, nobody is available to mock the squeak.{pause}That freedom feels efficient and unexpectedly lonely.

nodes.name: Errand B3
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Leg posts signs so quickly that two face the wrong direction.{pause}Chest buys the battery, then announces the receipt to an entire block.{pause}Silhouette reaches the bakery and fits twelve muffins into eleven slots.{pause}Each part solves its problem with a different kind of improvisation.{pause}Messages cross in the network, delayed by buildings and bus traffic.{pause}Four successful errands begin moving toward four different fountains.

nodes.name: Errand B4
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: Correction: use the fountain with the bronze fish, not the stone bird.{pause}Core turns around with the squeaky basket and no complaints.{pause}Leg retrieves both backward posters without blaming the wind.{pause}Chest lowers its voice before announcing the corrected location.{pause}Silhouette trades one muffin for directions from a crossing guard.{pause}They reach the proper fountain separately, proud and two minutes late.

nodes.name: Errand 11
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: The main tune returns as four clipboards receive four check marks.{pause}Books are here, posters are up, the battery works, and muffins survived.{pause}However, the reading corner needs shelves moved from the storage room.{pause}The singer needs a sound check before guests fill the square.{pause}The poster route forgot the north gate, and muffins need serving trays.{pause}The errands are finished, but the festival has begun needing Impulse.{pause}A fifth clipboard appears, and everyone pretends not to see it.

nodes.name: Errand 12
nodes.speaker: Strike Rouge
nodes.dialogue: Reassembly will give us one strong helper for every remaining job.{pause}Staying separate gives four small helpers with limited hands.{pause}Impulse tries a practice connection beside the fountain.{pause}Core meets Chest correctly, but Leg docks where the book bag belongs.{pause}Silhouette catches the muffins before the experiment becomes breakfast.{pause}Everyone agrees reassembly should wait until the square is calmer.

nodes.name: Errand 13
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The four Flyers take temporary stations around the festival.{pause}Core tows books to the shade and learns the squeaky wheel has fans.{pause}Chest powers the microphone and announces lost hats between songs.{pause}Leg tapes the north-gate poster to a fence that keeps moving.{pause}Silhouette guards muffins from pigeons and one determined coordinator.{pause}Separated, Impulse can hear four corners of the same happy noise.{pause}Core Flyer discovers the reading corner needs bookmarks, so children fold route-map scraps into{pause}bright little arrows.{pause}Chest Flyer lowers the microphone for a shy singer and learns that good sound support{pause}includes knowing when not to amplify.{pause}Leg Flyer redraws the north-gate poster after the wind sends three families confidently{pause}toward a locked equipment shed.{pause}Silhouette Flyer negotiates a muffin truce with the pigeons by relocating crumbs far{pause}beyond the festival tables.

nodes.name: Errand 14
nodes.speaker: Child
nodes.dialogue: Which part is the real Impulse? I need help reaching a book.{pause}All four Flyers answer at once, then become politely embarrassed.{pause}Core lowers the basket. Silhouette provides a stable step.{pause}Leg holds the poster tube as a railing while Chest reads the title.{pause}The child selects a space book and thanks every part individually.{pause}Impulse realizes being divided does not mean being less himself.

nodes.name: Errand 15
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Festival capacity reached. Component battery levels are falling.{pause}Core is tired from hauling books, and Leg has used nearly all tape.{pause}Chest's speaker crackles whenever somebody says raffle.{pause}Silhouette has muffin crumbs in an intake it did not know existed.{pause}Reassembly would share power and clear these small faults.{pause}Remaining separate would keep every busy station open through sunset.

nodes.name: Errand 16
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: I thought returning meant proving the split had ended correctly.{pause}Strike Rouge says returning can also mean coming back with stories.{pause}The title melody returns as each Flyer reports one favorite moment.{pause}Core liked the child choosing a book. Leg liked fixing the wrong signs.{pause}Chest liked the applause. Silhouette quietly liked guarding breakfast.{pause}Impulse decides the final shape should serve more than a checklist.{pause}The Flyers also report mistakes: one late book cart, one squealing speaker, two backward{pause}arrows, and a muffin with disputed ownership.{pause}None of those failures ruined the festival because somebody nearby adjusted before the whole{pause}team could reassemble.{pause}Impulse recognizes a form of coordination.{pause}It does not require every piece to occupy its assigned slot at the same moment.{pause}He records that lesson before the sunset decision makes it easy to forget.

nodes.name: Errand 17
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Sunset cleanup begins soon, and both options would help.{pause}Reassembled Impulse can move shelves, tables, and the heavy stage.{pause}Four Flyers can keep books, signs, sound, and snacks running longer.{pause}The first choice returns him to one body with a funny docking risk.{pause}The second extends the experiment and asks every part to cooperate.{pause}Impulse looks at the fountain reflection and chooses his Saturday.

nodes.name: Errand C1
nodes.speaker: Strike Rouge
nodes.dialogue: Color-map reassembly. Red meets red, white meets white.{pause}She clears the fountain plaza and places muffins beyond docking range.{pause}Core, Chest, Leg, and Silhouette hover at their marked corners.{pause}Impulse counts down slowly while the festival crowd counts with him.{pause}Four parts move inward, correct one wobble, and connect with a click.{pause}Applause erupts before anybody checks which way his feet face.

nodes.name: Errand C2
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: Systems stable. Books remembered. Muffin crumbs also remembered.{pause}He lifts the library shelves while Strike Rouge guides each corner.{pause}The squeaky basket follows behind like an honored support vehicle.{pause}Leg tape peels from his shoulder and sticks to the battery receipt.{pause}Chest announces cleanup at a voice level approved by nearby pigeons.{pause}One whole Impulse finishes jobs learned by four separate parts.

nodes.name: Errand C3
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: At the snack table, Impulse finds two muffins inside his feet.{pause}Silhouette packed them there during the hurried final checkpoint.{pause}He removes both carefully and declares them structurally unharmed.{pause}The coordinator places them on a plate marked COMPONENT RESERVE.{pause}Strike Rouge writes MUFFINS ARE NOT REASSEMBLY PARTS on the map.{pause}The warm ending tune plays as everyone shares the strange extras.

nodes.name: Errand C4
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: Four errands, one festival, and every component returned.{pause}The final report praises checkpoints, freedom, and color stickers.{pause}Impulse keeps the four clipboards tied together with a rubber band.{pause}Next Saturday, he volunteers before anyone can list the jobs.{pause}The bakery includes a box with twelve correctly separated slots.{pause}Impulse carries it in both hands and refuses to transform near lunch.

nodes.name: Errand D1
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: Independent service continues. Complaints go to the proper section.{pause}Core takes books, Chest takes sound, Leg takes signs, Silhouette snacks.{pause}Strike Rouge draws four charging routes around the fountain.{pause}The Flyers rotate stations so tired parts can rest without closing one.{pause}Students learn the schedule and wave when a new helper arrives.{pause}The festival stretches toward sunset without losing a single corner.

nodes.name: Errand D2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Core hosts story hour by projecting pages onto Chest's speaker panel.{pause}Leg turns spare poster tubes into rails for the reading corner.{pause}Silhouette serves muffins from the squeaky library basket.{pause}Chest announces raffle winners in a voice gentle enough for naps.{pause}Four specialized parts begin inventing jobs no clipboard mentioned.{pause}Strike Rouge replaces the reassembly map with a rotation chart.

nodes.name: Errand D3
nodes.speaker: Coordinator
nodes.dialogue: All four jobs are perfect. Please stay this way Saturday.{pause}Impulse agrees, but adds breaks, charging time, and one shared lunch.{pause}The coordinator signs four volunteer badges with the same name.{pause}Each Flyer wears one, though Leg's badge immediately catches tape.{pause}The evening tune follows four little lights around the darkening square.{pause}Nobody asks which badge belongs to the real Impulse anymore.

nodes.name: Errand D4
nodes.speaker: Impulse
nodes.dialogue: On future Saturdays, the fountain becomes his four-part checkpoint.{pause}Books arrive, posters point correctly, announcements stay friendly.{pause}Muffins travel in a box guarded by two extremely alert wings.{pause}At sunset, every part returns to share memories before reassembly.{pause}The final docking is private, careful, and completely pastry-free.{pause}Sunday's schedule contains one line: REST, ALL COMPONENTS.
